text:
Sam: heads up, running the eval harness locally with a quantized model is hanging during bring-up. reproduced on my laptop and in the mac CI runner.

Sam: command I ran:
```
./tools/eval-harness run --config tests/fixtures/quant-gpt2.yaml --model-path /mnt/models/gpt2-q4_0 --local
```

Sam: output stops at: 
```
INFO  model loader v0.9
INFO  quant profile: q4_0
INFO  allocating kv cache (8MB)
INFO  warming kv cache
[hang here indefinitely]
```

Neha: :eyes: I saw similar a week ago with q5 configs. For me it printed "warming kv cache" and then never progressed. Did you try --no-prefetch?

Sam: yep --no-prefetch still hangs. strace shows a futex sleep in the worker thread.

Ben: +1 that smells like a thread deadlock when quantized kernels switch to single-threaded fallbacks. Did you hit this in CI or only local?

Sam: both. CI job: run-eval-local-quant (mac-latest) failed with timeout once and then OOM (exit 137) on rerun.

ci-bot: Job run-eval-local-quant #432 failed: exit code 137. Rerun queued.

Aya: Also saw a flaky config validator exception when using that fixture: the harness config schema doesn't accept the new "quantize: q4_0" shorthand. You might get a confusing message like "expected object, got string" from the validator.

Sam: here's the validator output when I ran dry-run:
```
./tools/eval-harness run --dry-run -c tests/fixtures/quant-gpt2.yaml
ERROR  config validation failed: /model/quantize: expected object
  at /path/to/evalharness/config/schema.py:142
```

Neha: ouch. UX-wise we should accept either a string alias (q4_0) or a full object and show a helpful hint. The current traceback is not actionable for non-devs.

Ben: proposed short fixes:
- CLI: add --model-load-timeout and surface a failure if load > timeout
- Config validator: accept string shorthand for quantize and normalize internally
- Runner: add a watchdog thread that dumps stack traces on long sleeps (helps root-cause)
- CI: mark the mac job as retry-on-oom for now and add ulimit -v to avoid host-level OOM kills

Sam: I sketched a tiny patch to the CLI to add --model-load-timeout (default 30s). It returns exit code 4 with a clear message. Will open PR.

Dave: for the validator, we should update the schema or add a migration helper. I can take the validator change if Sam owns the CLI timeout.

Aya: can we also improve the error lines? Something like: "quantize: received 'q4_0' (string). Use quantize: { profile: 'q4_0' } or enable shorthand by setting config_version: 2" — that would be friendlier.

Ben: +1. Also add a small unit test for the shorthand and a flaky CI test that runs the quantized fixture under a short timeout to catch regressions.

Sam: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/210 (WIP) — adds --model-load-timeout and better error on timeout.

ci-bot: PR 210 created by Sam. Label: devex.

Neha: quick workaround: run with `ENV_EVAL_DEBUG=1 ./tools/eval-harness ...` — it prints thread dumps every 10s which helps triage. Also try `--batch-size 1` to avoid large mem reservations.

Sam: confirmed: setting --batch-size 1 made it progress past the hang on my laptop, probably avoided the path that deadlocks. Reproduces reliably with larger batches.

Dave: okay I'll take validator shorthand + improved error text. Ben you ok adding the unit + CI job?

Ben: yes, I'll add the unit and a flaky-catch workflow step.

Aya: can someone add a small doc blurb under docs/devex/local-runs.md about best practices for quantized bring-ups (env flags, --batch-size, --no-prefetch, debug env)? Saves time for new folks.

Sam: will add a quick note in the PR description and link to docs issue.

ci-bot: rerun for job run-eval-local-quant #433 started.

Sam: thanks all. I'll follow up when PR is ready for review.

Ben: thanks — sounds like a plan. :thumbsup:
